historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: The envelope claim — interior fuel belt from 300–500 m valley floors to ~2 100 m treeline, Big White ~2 320 m — is asserted in prose with no source. It is checkable and probably right, but it is uncited, and it is the justification for the single most expensive number in the model.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: The single load-bearing assumption in the project. Nothing constrains it; it was chosen. Everything below inherits from it. See §1.1.

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: 2 194.7 m³/t gives exactly 5.00%; 2 200 is the round number above it. Verified by sweep: 2 000 → −4.31%, 2 100 → +0.47%, 2 200 → +5.25%.

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Presented as a result ("the margin is +5.25% on all three classes") when it is an input: a 5% requirement divided by a rounding. It is identical across classes only because m_dry = m_pay is identical across classes, so the "no class needed an exception" line is a restatement of the assumption, not a check on it. The arithmetic is right; the framing is not.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Volume matches a prolate spheroid to better than 0.2%, which is checkable and checks out. Fineness 4 is a choice; it sets frontal area and therefore drag.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: The requirement is real and independently motivated. The 7.2% headroom over it is not derived, and the round-number-per-payload result (1.55 payloads exactly) suggests it was chosen for tidiness. `selftest.js` asserts `ln2CapT ≥ needT` — a tautology, since one was set from the other. It can only fail if someone edits one and not the other, which is a useful regression guard and not evidence.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Labelled "demonstration assumption, not a plant spec". Industrial nitrogen liquefaction is in this band, but no source is given and none is in the repository.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: The arithmetic reproduces (6 505 MWh ÷ (24 − 3) MW = 310 h). It rests entirely on 200 W/m² applied twenty-four hours a day. The document says so — "a real recovery is several times longer again" — but publishes the optimistic number as the headline. See §1.5.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Arithmetic solid; `cryoMW` = 6/30/100 MW has no derivation anywhere.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Only constraint is `selftest` requiring it < 1. Moves the P-10000's cycle by ±2.2% and the two smaller classes by nothing at all, because their recovery is discarded (see the energy section).
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: The inversion is exact and round-trips in `tests/cases/sim-physics.cases.js`. Its inputs are `battMW`, `genMW`, `diskM2`, `propEta`, `rhoAir` — four assumptions and one arbitrary constant.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_value_text: rotors carry 1/0.6 of their thrust budget
historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Nothing anywhere states why 60%. It is the difference between the descent closing and not closing, and it appears again in `state.js` as the upper end of a hand-drawn `share` schedule.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: See §1 and the closing note. Chosen so a force balance closed at the ceiling; the balance now happens at the source, where it does not close (12 666 t of capacity against 13 723 t of hold). The comment asserting it still closes is live in `sim/config.js:230`. Sensitivity today: ±20% moves cycle energy by ∓0.4%. A number reverse-engineered from a result it no longer produces, controlling nothing.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Same origin, same problem, and measurably worse: ±20% moves *every* published figure by 0.0%.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: The bag is 90.4 / 91.5 / 92.2% of the hold it is then shown to solve. Measured: the bag needed for `retainedT = 0` is 55 t on a P-1000 and **1 099 t** on a P-10000 — 8% of the surplus, not 90%. The other 82% is bought purely to shrink the letdown term. Nothing states a stopping rule, and the choice halves the headline energy. See §1.3.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Justified against `anchorFromAglM` (below) "with margin". The margin is not stated. Sets the winch time floor on `SOURCE_APPROACH`, which does not bind on any class.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: 440 mm at 850 m and ~970 kg/m³ does give 125 t, so the two numbers are consistent. 122 MN over that section is ~800 MPa, which is inside what UHMWPE rope achieves but implies a safety factor around 2 that is never stated. **The 125 t is explicitly not charged as dry mass anywhere** — the project says so, which is the right thing to do with a known omission.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Both constants are unjustified. The 15 m is a fixed lift height applied to bags whose diameters are 6.2 m and 28.7 m — 2.4× the small bag's diameter and 0.52× the large one's — so it cannot be the "lift needed to break the surface" it is described as. The 0.85 winch efficiency has no source. The term is small (1.4% of the P-10000's cycle) but it is the number that makes the whole mechanism look free, quoted as "fifty-eight to one" against the rotor work it removes.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Applied to drag *and* disc power, which are different machines. Largest single tunable effect on energy: −20% → +14.2% on the P-10000.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: The best-defended assumption in the file: C_dv = 0.024, and a Reynolds/flat-plate estimate puts skin friction at 37% of the assumed total, which is a sane split for a fineness-4 hull. The document then says plainly that it is a *bare hull* figure charging nothing for 14 rotor installations, fins or the hose pod.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_value_text: **1.10 kg/m³** for drag and every rotor calculation
historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Described as "a fixed working-band density". There is no such band: the hulls are sized at 0.9569 and fill at 1.0793. `config.js:24`, `PHYSICS.md` §11 and `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` §1 all state it is "ISA at about 990 m"; it is ISA at **1 107 m** (`altitudeForDensity(1.10)` — run it). The stated consequences, drag overstated 15% and induced power understated 7%, are correct. Measured effect on the P-10000's cycle energy: ±20% → ±10.4%, eight times what `PHYSICS.md` §10 reports.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: The exponent is the whole story and it is real: thrust^1.5 means the last 10% of the hold costs 3.2% of the full rotor power. That is a genuine and well-explained piece of physics. What the rotors are asked to hold is chosen, not derived.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Lumps pump, motor, drive, hose friction and residual kinetic energy. `PHYSICS.md` §5 states the omission that matters: a 1.78 m bore at 15 m³/s, and a 250 m standing column of that bore weighing 625 t that the mass ledger never carries.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Good design decision: hose length *is* the fill altitude *is* the pumping head, one number, so they cannot disagree. They previously did.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: No justification anywhere for any of the three. It sets `WATER_FILL` and, since the single-pass change, `WATER_RELEASE` as well — 22.2 of the P-10000's 45.5 cycle minutes, 49% of the cycle. See §1.4.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: `hoseDeployMin` = 4/6/10 and the 0.5 and 1.5 are all unjustified.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: The trapezoid correction is right in principle — a leg is not a step — but 15% accelerating and 15% braking is chosen. It inflates every transit leg by 17.6%.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Nothing derives them. −20% costs the P-10000 8.2% of throughput and saves 17.8% of energy; +20% buys 6.3% of throughput for 26.5% more energy.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Verified: the drop-line term gives 1.78 / 3.03 / 5.13 min against fill-limited 3.33 / 5.56 / 11.11, so the metering rate binds on every class. `dropKm` therefore changes no published figure at all today — ±20% moves energy and throughput by 0.0%, against the ±2.1% / ±6.6% in `PHYSICS.md` §10.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: A round number.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: A literal, correctly described as one. The reasoning for going from three passes to one — an 876 m hull should not reverse over the fire it is dropping on, and the water lands on the same line either way — is sound.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Bounded above by `dropSeg()` shrinking the line to fit the fire, which is a real constraint; the values themselves are chosen.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: The *shape* is right — a ship does not climb to 1 500 m on a two-minute hop — and the fix it replaced (a P-1000 diving at 44 m/s) was real. The constants are picked.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Twelve unjustified numbers. A test in `sim-plan.cases.js` says outright that "the mode ordering has flipped five times and is not load-bearing", which is the honest way to carry them.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_value_text: "transit distance" on all three at 15 km
historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: The 0.25-payload retention threshold and the 0.92-of-bus `battLimited` threshold are unjustified. Two of the five bottleneck strings (`descent authority`, `descent ballast`) are unreachable on shipped numbers; `cryogenic production rate` fires in endurance mode on a flag that is true in all 135 grid cases and therefore carries no information.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Six thresholds, no derivation. Monotonicity is tested; the values are not defended.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: The exponent, the cap and the discount shape are all chosen. The *principle* — a fleet drawing full payloads from a pond beside a lake is the wrong picture — is sound.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: The `max(0, …)` silently destroys energy on the two smaller classes: **0.303 MWh discarded on a P-100 whose entire cycle is 1.308 MWh, and 0.594 MWh on a P-1000**. On those classes the published pumping bill is *zero* — the least contentious number in the model does not appear in their headline energy at all. This is a defect and it is not on the list of six.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Drag on a streamlined body does not depend on how much water is inside it. The comment "lighter ship, cheaper leg" is not a mechanism at this level of model. The 0.55 removes 4.26 MWh from the P-10000's cycle.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Correctly identified, correctly quantified, and now defused rather than fixed: it was 45% of the cycle before the bag. The cap is inactive below ~55 km one-way, so in practice the term is a bare 0.2 fraction. The `battLimited` interaction still runs backwards (a "longer, shallower letdown" *raises* the energy), and is now unreachable, which is worse than broken.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: See the anchor row.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Hotel load is 2% of `genMW` — 2.276 MWh, 5.3% of the cycle, no derivation. The 0.4 drag multiplier removes a further 12.62 MWh.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Charging drag at full rate on every phase gives **59.90 MWh instead of 43.02** (+39.2%), and **5.99 kWh/t instead of 4.30**. On the P-1000 it is +23.3%, on the P-100 +13.2%. Two unexplained numbers set 39% of the flagship energy claim. See §1.2.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: No derivation, no source, no dial, six copies, and — checked — **not in `sim/config.js`**, which the README's table calls the home of "every assumption, in one file". It is a peak-ish figure (≈20% efficiency at 1 000 W/m² insolation) applied continuously. `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` §0 admits "a real recovery is several times longer again" and then publishes the optimistic figure anyway.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Computed against hull geometry: 85.5% / 86.5% / 79.6% of *planform* area. Near-total upper-surface coverage, chosen.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: Defect 6, correctly identified as the most consequential item. Measured: removing `genMW` from `rotorMaxT` cuts rotor capacity by 14.6% / 14.6% / 6.6%. Crediting it as energy at full output gives 4.6 / 23.6 / **113.8 MWh** per cycle against spends of 1.31 / 6.98 / 43.02. The generators would cover every cycle on every class.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: `PHYSICS.md` §3 does the damaging arithmetic itself: at 250 Wh/kg the battery is 80% of the P-10000's entire dry allowance, and the 3D library's own mass split implies 1 430 Wh/kg. The two halves of the project do not agree and the document says so.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

historical_audit_rows.historical_assessment_text: No sizing argument of any kind. It is a stage set.
historical_audit_rows.interpretation: Dated audit row, not a fresh sensitivity measurement or necessarily an independent constant

current_source_locations.source_text: Illustration: the dry-mass budget sizes an assumed UHMWPE cable by minimum break strength, not by diameter. Design load including pickup is bag-water weight under the quasi-static pickup assumption; dynamic snatch, cable self-weight and bag/rigging dry weight are omitted. Required minimum break strength is that load times the safety factor. Assumption: credible safety factor 5; assumption: floor safety factor 3; assumption: demonstrated safety factor 7. Assumption: credible minimum-strength-per-linear-density coefficient 1.5 MN per kg/m; assumption: floor coefficient 2.0 MN per kg/m; assumption: demonstrated coefficient 1.4 MN per kg/m. Those columns do not qualify a rope product. The bottom-up dry-mass budget charges the installed cable, bag and winch. The flight model still assumes dry mass equals payload; it does not integrate that equipment bill. Terminations, wear, creep, cyclic pickup and the bag load path remain unqualified. See `research/analysis/mass-budget.py` and its generated records.
# budget cases, not proof that an anchor cable has been demonstrated.
"credible": (1.5e6, "Assumed minimum-strength coefficient, not a selected rope product."),
"demonstrated": (1.4e6, "Assumed lower coefficient; no anchor rope has been qualified."),
# Dynamic snatch, cable/bag dry weight and termination/wear/creep allowances are absent.
# Minimum break strength = this design load times the assumed safety factor.
# Bag wetted area and the winch's assumed lift speed price separate mass lines.
lin = pull_n * ev("rope_safety_factor", case) / ev("rope_n_per_kg_per_m", case)
f"{pull_n / 1e6:.1f} MN quasi-static pickup load at SF {ev('rope_safety_factor', case):.0f}",
"Assumed minimum break strength = design load x safety factor; cable self-weight, "
"dynamic snatch and terminations omitted. No rope product or diameter qualified.")

named_input_groups.consumption_and_history: The current bottom-up dry-mass budget uses quasi-static pickup load times rope_safety_factor, divided by rope_n_per_kg_per_m, times configured cable length. These coefficients price an assumed cable mass. Cable self-weight, dynamic snatch and bag/rigging dry weight are excluded from pickup design load; terminations, wear, creep and cyclic pickup remain unqualified. The flight ledger still assumes dryT=payloadT and does not integrate this equipment bill.
named_input_groups.evidence_needed: Selected installed rope/construction/lot and loadbearing geometry; measured strength per linear density, terminations, dynamic pickup including carried/self weights, service/environment/creep/wear/fatigue evidence and explicit application-specific margin-policy justification. A safety-factor label alone does not qualify the cable.
